provenance_legend.wrapper: Every numeric pharmacological value is an object with keys: value, unit, range, cv_percent, n, distribution, provenance.

provenance.status.CITED: A real source states this value. source, url, quote (the value as the source words it), retrieved and tier are all populated.
provenance.status.ESTIMATED: Derived or assumed. provenance.note carries the one-line justification. No source/url.
provenance.status.NOT_FOUND: Searched and not found. value is null; provenance.note says what was looked for and where.

provenance.tier.1: Regulatory product labeling (FDA SPL via DailyMed/openFDA, EMA SmPC).
provenance.tier.3: Curated chemical/drug database (PubChem, ChEMBL, DrugBank, DrugCentral).
provenance.tier.4: Secondary web summary. Used only where tiers 1-3 failed, and marked as such.

provenance_legend.units: hours (_h), mg, ng/mL, L, L/h, mmHg, mmol/L. Fractions are 0-1 except fields named _percent.
provenance_legend.null_policy: null means absent. Never 0, never 'N/A'. Keys are never omitted.
provenance_legend.variability_policy: range and cv_percent are populated wherever the source supports them. Where a source gives mean +/- SD, cv_percent is computed as 100*SD/mean and provenance.note says so. Where only a min-max range is published, cv_percent is ESTIMATED by treating the range as an approximate 95% interval of a lognormal, and provenance.note shows the arithmetic.

clinical_effect.dose_response_slope: Label-cited, qualitative but directionally firm: (a) 'An antihypertensive effect of lisinopril was seen with 5 mg of lisinopril in some patients. However, in both studies blood pressure reduction occurred sooner and was greater in patients treated with 10 mg, 20 mg or 80 mg of lisinopril than patients treated with 5 mg'; (b) from Dosage and Administration: 'Doses up to 80 mg have been used but do not appear to give greater effect' beyond the usual 20-40 mg/day range. So: steep between 5 and 10-20 mg, essentially FLAT from 40 to 80 mg. A saturating Emax curve with ED50 well below the usual dose is the right shape; a linear dose-effect term would be wrong at the top of the range.

simulation_hooks.why_this_drug: The long-half-life, hepatically-cleared, purely vascular drug. Its 30-50 h half-life and 7-8 day approach to steady state force the engine to handle multi-day horizons and accumulation, which the other two never exercise. Its oedema data is the only fully dose-resolved adverse-effect curve in B1's dataset and the most visually compelling thing to animate. And it is the counterexample on renal impairment: no adjustment, versus lisinopril's mandatory one.

substances.record_notes: STRONGEST parts: the dose-resolved oedema incidence table (1.8/3.0/10.8% at 2.5/5/10 mg with a 0.6% placebo rate) and the sex split (14.6% women vs 5.6% men) are the best-quantified adverse-effect data in B1's dataset; the placebo-corrected 12/6 mmHg standing BP reduction at 24 h postdose is the best-sourced efficacy number; the baseline-dependency multiplier (1.5x for moderate vs mild hypertension) and the cited near-zero effect in normotensive subjects (+1/-2 mmHg) give the PD model both a slope and a floor; and logP is confirmed at 3.00 by three independent sources. WEAKEST parts: (1) *** Vd and CL are both ESTIMATED and are the least certain numbers in this record *** — the US label gives no volume of distribution at all, the widely-quoted 21 L/kg could not be traced to a primary or EMA source within the timebox (medicines.org.uk returned HTTP 404), and CL is derived from it, so both inherit that uncertainty; they are internally consistent with the label's half-life and with commonly reported concentrations, which is corroboration but not citation. (2) No Cmax or AUC anchor exists in the label, so absolute concentrations are model-derived. (3) No numeric BP figures per dose level, so the efficacy dose-response shape is assumed while the adverse-effect dose-response is cited — an asymmetry worth stating openly. (4) No numeric exposure ratio exists for amlodipine with any STRONG CYP3A inhibitor in any label; the only quantitative evidence there is epidemiologic (AKI odds ratio 1.61) and must not be converted into an exposure multiplier.

cross_agent_notes.for_agent_B2_schema: Follow research/B1-notes.md section 1. Same Val wrapper, same provenance/tier keys, same units. Write data/substances_part2.json with the identical top-level shape; the lead concatenates the `substances` arrays.
for_agent_C_rules: Lisinopril + HCTZ potassium interaction is quantified in one trial, same units: lisinopril alone gives mean K+ +0.1 mmol/L with 15% of patients above +0.5; with HCTZ the mean flips to -0.1 with only 4% above +0.5 and 12% below -0.5. The cleanest drug-drug numbers in this dataset.

Amlodipine + simvastatin is a HARD DOSE CAP, not a warning: 'Do not exceed ZOCOR 20 mg once daily' (Zocor 2.5) and 'Limit the dose of simvastatin in patients on amlodipine to 20 mg daily' (Norvasc 7.7). Simvastatin AUC x1.77.

DO NOT create renal milligram caps for losartan or amlodipine. Both labels explicitly state no renal dose adjustment is needed, despite losartan exposure rising 50-90% in renal impairment. Only lisinopril has a real renal dosing rule (halve initial dose at CrCl 10-30; 2.5 mg below 10 or on dialysis).

POSITIVE rules available: amlodipine + beta-blocker is explicitly safe (no AV conduction effect, no adverse ECG changes in trials) — the product should say so rather than warn. Amlodipine + grapefruit juice has NO interaction per the label, so declining to warn is correct. Amlodipine + atorvastatin is fine while amlodipine + simvastatin is capped, so statin choice is a recommendable action.

Amlodipine effect is reported as similar in Black and white patients, whereas both RAAS drugs report a smaller effect in Black patients. Model via baseline renin status rather than a race checkbox — both labels supply the low-renin explanation themselves.

Losartan's uricosuric (urate-lowering) effect is NOT QUANTIFIED anywhere in B1's sources. It is a stated reason the drug is in the set and it anchors the contrast with HCTZ's gout reject case. Source a magnitude before writing that rule.

No CPIC or DPWG guideline exists for losartan/CYP2C9 or for amlodipine (both verified absent). Only metoprolol/CYP2D6 has one (CPIC 2024). Do not imply guideline backing for genotype-based losartan or amlodipine dosing.
for_agent_E_simulation: Losartan MUST be modelled as a parent-metabolite pair. The metabolite EXP3174 has t1/2 7.4 h vs the parent's 2.1 h and is 10-40x more potent; the parent alone cannot justify once-daily dosing.

The label volumes of distribution for losartan (34 L) and EXP3174 (12 L) are Vss and are mutually INCONSISTENT with the same labels' clearance and half-life under a one-compartment model. Derived Vz values of 109 L and 32 L are supplied in the records; use those for one-compartment work.

Peak-to-trough ratios span four orders of magnitude across B1's drugs: amlodipine 1.30, lisinopril 2.7, EXP3174 6.8, losartan parent ~2000. All derived from cited half-lives. This is the quantitative backbone of the concentration-time animation.

Amlodipine needs 7-8 days to reach steady state and accumulates ~2.9-fold; lisinopril and losartan reach steady state within a day and do not accumulate. A 24-hour-only simulation will materially understate amlodipine.
Lisinopril's PD onset is 1 h but its plasma tmax is 7 h. A direct-effect PD model cannot reproduce this; an effect compartment or turnover model is required.

COMBINATION ANCHOR, fully cited and in matched units: losartan 50 mg alone gives 5.5-10.5/3.5-7.5 mmHg placebo-adjusted; losartan 50 mg + HCTZ 12.5 mg gives 15.5/9.2 mmHg. The lisinopril/HCTZ label independently describes the combination as 'approximately additive'. Anchor the composition rule on these.
Amlodipine response scales with baseline BP (1.5x for moderate vs mild hypertension) and is near zero in normotensive subjects (+1/-2 mmHg). Use the normotensive figure as a boundary test.
Losartan's maximal effect takes 3-6 weeks to develop, so a purely concentration-driven model will over-predict day 1 and under-predict week 6. Relevant to the 5-year prognosis feature.
for_agent_F_organ_map: Best mechanistic contrast in the dataset: lisinopril LOWERS angiotensin II (blocks synthesis) while losartan RAISES it (blocks the receptor). Same BP outcome, opposite movement of the intermediate. Showing this proves the model is mechanistic rather than a lookup table.
Second best: the bradykinin/cough channel is lit for lisinopril (2.5% excess cough) and explicitly dark for losartan (label states it does not affect the bradykinin response).

Third: in the kidney, lisinopril dilates the EFFERENT arteriole and transiently LOWERS GFR, while amlodipine dilates the AFFERENT arteriole and RAISES GFR. Same organ, opposite direction, different arteriole.
Highest-impact adverse animation: amlodipine peripheral oedema, dose-resolved (1.8/3.0/10.8% at 2.5/5/10 mg) and sex-resolved (14.6% women vs 5.6% men). Bind ankle swelling directly to that curve.

None of B1's three drugs changes heart rate — all three labels say so explicitly (lisinopril 'no compensatory tachycardia', losartan 'essentially no change', amlodipine +0.3 bpm). Metoprolol is the only heart-rate actor in the set, so the heart animation's motion belongs to Agent B2's drug.
verdict_on_team_draft_scope_1_3: 'Lisinopril 5-40 mg' — PARTIALLY CORRECT. The 40 mg ceiling is right (label: doses up to 80 mg 'do not appear to give greater effect'), but the label's starting dose is 10 mg once daily; 5 mg is the start only for patients already on a diuretic, and the usual range is 20-40 mg/day.

'Losartan 25-100 mg' — CONFIRMED. Label: start 50 mg, maximum 100 mg, start 25 mg if volume-depleted or in mild-moderate hepatic impairment. The label adds that 150 mg gives no greater effect than 50-100 mg, so the cap is an efficacy plateau.
'Amlodipine 2.5-10 mg' — CONFIRMED exactly. Label: start 5 mg, maximum 10 mg, start 2.5 mg in small/fragile/elderly patients or hepatic insufficiency.

'Verapamil often avoided in heart failure' (step 3, item 3) — CONFIRMED and worth keeping, but note the corollary the draft does not state: amlodipine is NOT in that category. Its label documents no negative inotropic effect at therapeutic doses and no AV conduction effect even with beta-blockers, which is exactly why dihydropyridines are acceptable in heart failure while verapamil is not.
'ACE/ARB contraindicated in pregnancy' (step 3, item 8) — CONFIRMED. Both lisinopril and losartan carry BOXED WARNINGS for fetal toxicity. Two of the dataset's hard reject cases.

'ACE/ARB first-line and renal-protective in CKD' (step 3, item 2) — CONFIRMED in direction, but flag for Agent C: the labels do NOT support combining an ACE inhibitor with an ARB. VA NEPHRON-D (losartan + lisinopril, the exact pair in this dataset) was STOPPED EARLY for safety with no efficacy benefit — hyperkalaemia 6.3 vs 2.6 and acute kidney injury 12.2 vs 6.7 events per 100 person-years.
